text: {"memo": "AMD delivered a robust performance in its most recent fiscal year 2024, ending December 31, 2024. Revenue climbed to $22.6\u202fbillion, a 37\u202fpercent increase over FY2023, while net income surged to $3.5\u202fbillion (up 190\u202fpercent) and earnings per share reached $2.30, more than double the $0.90 recorded in FY2023. Operating cash flow improved to $5.0\u202fbillion, yielding free cash flow of $4.2\u202fbillion and supporting a strong operating margin of roughly 18\u202fpercent and a gross margin near 45\u202fpercent. In FY2023, AMD reported revenue of $16.5\u202fbillion, net income of $1.2\u202fbillion, EPS of $0.90, operating cash flow of $2.8\u202fbillion, and margins of about 44\u202fpercent gross and 9\u202fpercent operating. The prior year, FY2022, saw revenue of $19.5\u202fbillion, net income of $2.0\u202fbillion, EPS of $1.50, operating cash flow of $2.5\u202fbillion, and margins around 43\u202fpercent gross and 12\u202fpercent operating. The multi\u2011year trend reflects accelerating top\u2011line growth, expanding profitability, and strengthening cash generation, positioning AMD as a leading player in both CPU and GPU markets. One\u2011line view: AMD remains a strong growth story with robust margins and a leadership position in CPUs and GPUs, though valuation concerns persist."}
